svg.title: KTL Federation: a domain context layer
svg.desc: Bottom to top. Five member bundles, Knowledge Trust Ladder (the KTL skills) at w3id.org/ktl/knowledge/, KTL Curator (the curator's assistant in Obsidian) at w3id.org/ktl/curator/knowledge/, KTL Registrar (the registrar role in Obsidian) at w3id.org/ktl/registrar/knowledge/, AI-LinkMO (operational AI governance) at noelmcloughlin.github.io/ai-linkmo/knowledge/ and gist (Semantic Arts' upper ontology in LinkML) at w3id.org/lmodel/gist/knowledge/, are each built and curated in their own repository on their own trust ladder, drawn as a small ladder and three pills reading derived, checked and confirmed: green for what an agent derived, gold for what deterministic tools checked, blue for what a named person confirmed. Each member releases its bundle with the KTL sidecar to GitHub Releases as a zip with its .sha256 and a build attestation, and nothing in a zip is edited. The domain is this repository's bundle at https://w3id.org/ktl/federation/knowledge/: members/, whose concepts name one release each by its zip and checksum and which a person confirms; policies/federation, what admits a bundle, what a member adds and the diamond rule; and domains/ktl-federation, the Domain concept where this build starts, with unowned_targets fail and no max_depth set, so the default of three tiers applies. Each member concept is part of the Domain concept, which relates to the policy. Another domain may name this one as a MemberDomain, and its own build starts there. On each release of the domain, knowledge-federate.py builds the workspace: this domain's context layer, one named graph per member's base_iri plus the lock as DCAT and VoID, served under w3id.org/ktl/federation/workspace/, where a link no member owns fails the build and every trust label is computed on read. At the top, readers - agents through the lokf-registry MCP server, SPARQL clients and people on the site - read index.md first and traverse on demand.
